clusters.name: Your grandfather Gordon's death, 1991–1992
clusters.reason: Around your grandfather Gordon's stroke in June 1991, within the next year: your wrist injury stopped your playing that October with your anxiety and functioning both down, Rafe moved out after a blow-up in November, you were on your own getting high and absorbed in fixing radios by late November, and by January 1992 you were lost and low, unable to get going. In those same months your mother's move to the rebuilt house on Hollin Road and the household becoming crowded with Desmond's children sit nearby. Your exchange to Portugal in early 1994 is where you found your drive again; the period settles there.

clusters.name: Your grandmother Winifred found to have bowel cancer, 2001–2004
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Winifred's bowel cancer diagnosis in 2001 or 2002, within the next two years: you were running out of steam for performing in September 2001 with your anxiety up and functioning down, you had a disastrous audition for the national orchestra in early 2002 and were done with performing, you were on poor terms with your family and friends and left Thornbury for Gull Harbour in autumn 2002. You met Marisol at a winter party in early 2003, left Gull Harbour to live with her in Fenwick by June, then split up within the year and sank into deep depression once back in Thornbury that winter, unable to face your family. You could not face your parents, and relied on friends instead; Corbin spoke with your dad during your stay. Your grandmother died in February 2004 while you were at the airport; you visited her sickroom briefly and hung over on the way, and by January 2004 you had requested help from your parents with therapy costs and returned to your therapist. The period settles as your recovery began to point you toward nursing.

clusters.name: Your grandmother Lorna's death, 2008
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Lorna's death in January 2008, within the next year: you were at Alder Creek building with Silas in July 2008, too drained for conversation with your mother, and she pressed you to visit despite your saying the timing was wrong. The visit went wrong; you kept the door shut on her. You then left for nursing school at Marlow Sound in September and stopped speaking to your mother; the silence held for roughly a year. Every shift in these months is yours, and no one else's shows then.

clusters.name: Your partner Wren's mother Frances's retirement, 2019–2020
clusters.reason: Around your marriage to Wren in March 2017 and the pace of her family's life, within the next few years: by October 2019 you said you saw your mother a bit less once Wren came along. In October 2019 Wren was swamped one thing after another with a street party, a fundraising dinner, and the drive to the lake for her mother Frances's retirement party; your anxiety was up and functioning down. You were too strict laying out a plan to settle her when she was swamped, and she talked with her father and brother all day with nothing happening to one that the others don't hear. Once the weekend had a plan she settled, her anxiety down and functioning up. At the lake weekend itself in late October you awoke from the small hours with no more sleep, could only pull back as the others rose, and felt you don't belong; Wren was anxious when you'd had no sleep at family occasions, with long quiet drives home afterward. Your grandmother Alice was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis in October 2017; your cousin Bella was treated for melanoma in early 1994. The period settles once the weekend was over and the family returned home.

periods.name: the year I left home
periods.words: The first is the year I left home: I went off to the conservatory, hurt my wrist in the first term and couldn't play, dropped out and drifted at my mother's place, then spent a bleak spell at the community college shooting pool every night until an exchange in Portugal snapped me out of it and I tore through the rest of my coursework.

periods.name: the long slump
periods.words: The second is the long slump, roughly ages 27 to 29, when nothing at home felt right, I moved to Gull Harbour away from nearly everyone I knew, then followed Marisol to Fenwick, and when that fell apart I went under, a depression I only really climbed out of after nursing school.
